summary: Published person attention retains subject-keyed source folds and presentation dependencies. A changed ask, custom source or agent prompt rebuilds only its affected source subjects and cards; shared login, review, hold, drift and broken-gate sources rebuild only on relevant input changes. Unread commits do not rebuild attention sources, and unchanged attention no longer reevaluates on a periodic clock.

replay.detail: No replay or durable state conversion. Retained source snapshots are volatile and full rebuilds remain authoritative after checkpoint or projection resets.

schema.detail: No persisted schema or public client protocol change. Internal attention deltas carry changed subjects and source kinds; publications retain source snapshots and per-card presentation dependencies.

rules.detail: Attention eligibility and ownership rules are unchanged. Clock wakes use actual source admission, future-claim boundaries and native prompt answer-window expiry instead of a periodic reevaluation interval. Future admission does not age a current prompt's answerability; only its exact expiry rebuilds that prompt.

compatibility.detail: Existing attention clients keep the same rows and ordering. Duplicate host-hold source collection is removed. Mail input routing seeks later legacy runtime claims through the existing kind index rather than scanning unrelated batch history for each changed claim; invalidation semantics and persisted indexes are unchanged.

downtime.detail: Ordinary rolling deployment; source snapshots initialize from a complete fold.

manual.detail: Production attention_work counters attribute cards_presented, cards_enriched, subjects_rebuilt and groups_rebuilt. Deterministic regression coverage exercises one changed ask, one changed agent prompt, unread commits and exact clock admissions without timer-based source rebuilding.

recovery.detail: Checkpoint invalidation, graph projection resets and older cuts use the full source rebuild path rather than retaining stale folds.
